title: Hardcoded AWS-format access key committed to source
detail: Line 13 declares `const metricsToken = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"`. The value matches the AWS IAM access key ID pattern (`AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}`). Committing credentials in source permanently embeds them in the version history and exposes them to every reader of the repository. Even if this specific value is a documentation placeholder, the pattern teaches callers to supply a real key in the same position, making future accidental commits likely. Gitleaks did not flag this value (it is on the gitleaks example-key allowlist); the finding is based on manual inspection.

title: TLS certificate verification disabled in HTTP client (InsecureSkipVerify: true)
detail: `newClient()` at lines 15–20 constructs an `http.Client` whose `TLSClientConfig` sets `InsecureSkipVerify: true`. This suppresses all certificate validation — expired, self-signed, or fraudulent certificates are silently accepted. Any caller using this client is therefore susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks that can intercept or alter traffic, including any token or credential it carries. Semgrep flagged the same `tls.Config` block under the adjacent `missing-ssl-minversion` rule (see separate finding).

title: OS command injection via exec.Command("sh","-c",...) with unsanitised instance parameter
detail: `Console()` constructs a shell command at line 24 using `fmt.Sprintf("virsh console %s", instance)` and executes it through `exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...)`. Because the command is interpreted by a shell, any shell metacharacter in `instance` (e.g. `;`, `|`, `$(...)`, `` ` ``) allows execution of arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. `instance` is a caller-supplied function parameter with no sanitisation visible in this file. Semgrep did not flag this pattern with the rulesets used (`p/security-audit`, `p/owasp-top-ten`).

title: TLS MinVersion not set — minimum TLS version relies on Go runtime default
detail: The `tls.Config` at line 17 does not set `MinVersion`, meaning the minimum TLS version is governed by the Go runtime default (TLS 1.2 as of Go 1.22). While TLS 1.2 is currently acceptable, omitting an explicit `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13` leaves the floor open to future Go default changes or library misuse. This finding is informational in the context of the same config block already setting `InsecureSkipVerify: true`, which completely disables certificate validation regardless. Flagged by semgrep `missing-ssl-minversion` (WARNING).
